mainTopic: The end of the story of רבה בר אבוה and אליהו, and the laws of returning a borrower's collateral.
overview: The amud finishes the story of רבה בר אבוה and אליהו הנביא. אליהו gives the source that a naked person may not separate תרומה, and explains that a כהן may stand among graves of non-Jews because, according to רבי שמעון בן יוחי, they do not give over טומאה. רבה בר אבוה admits that the pressure of earning a living keeps him from learning. אליהו brings him into גן עדן to gather leaves, but he throws them away when a voice warns that he is using up his עולם הבא. The scent left in his cloak still sells for a fortune, which he gives to his sons-in-law. The גמרא then turns to the laws of collateral. רב ששת explains that a poor man's collateral may not stay with the lender overnight, but a rich man's may. רב ששת and רבא give two different readings of a confusing ברייתא about taking and returning collateral. רבא corrects רב שיזבי's teaching so that a day garment is returned for the day and a night garment for the night. Finally, רבי יוחנן rules that after the debtor dies, the creditor may take the collateral from the children. The גמרא begins a challenge to him from רבי מאיר, and that challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Where do we learn that a naked person may not separate תרומה?
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר אבוה asks אליהו for the source that a naked person may not separate תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that a naked person may not separate תרומה?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר אבוה asks אליהו another question in their ongoing conversation. He wants the source for why a naked person may not separate תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He is not asking whether the rule exists. He already knows it and wants its source in the תורה. Separating תרומה comes with a ברכה, which makes it an act of holiness.

keyTerms.meaning: Separate תרומה (the כהן's portion of produce)

phrases.english: From where do we know that a naked person may not separate תרומה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of questions רבה בר אבוה is asking אליהו.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that forbids a naked person to separate תרומה.

steps.title: The source is the פסוק about seeing nakedness
steps.stepSummary: אליהו answers with the פסוק 'And He shall not see any nakedness in you.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And He shall not see any nakedness in you.'
steps.whatsHappening: אליהו answers with a פסוק. It teaches that holy words may not be said where there is uncovered nakedness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says that nakedness must not be 'seen' among the people while they are in a state of holiness. Separating תרומה comes with a ברכה, so it is a holy act. A naked person therefore may not do it.

phrases.english: As it is written: “And He shall not see any nakedness in you.”

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'וְלֹא יִרְאֶה בְךָ עֶרְוַת דָּבָר' forbids holy acts, like separating תרומה with a ברכה, in front of nakedness.

steps.title: Why is a כהן standing in a cemetery?
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר אבוה challenges אליהו: you are a כהן, so how can you stand in a cemetery?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Isn't the Master a כהן? Why is the Master standing in a cemetery?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר אבוה points out that a כהן may not become טמא from the dead. So how can אליהו stand in a cemetery?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sentence is phrased as a question, but it works as a challenge. It assumes that every grave gives over טומאת מת, which would forbid a כהן to be there. The answer in the next step will question that assumption.

keyTerms.meaning: A priest, who may not become טמא from a dead body

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָאו כֹּהֵן הוּא מָר?
phrases.english: He said to him: Isn't the Master a כהן?

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא קָאֵי מָר בְּבֵית הַקְּבָרוֹת!
phrases.english: What is the reason the Master is standing in a cemetery!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָאו כֹּהֵן הוּא מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic in the conversation.
steps.kashyaTarget: אליהו's behavior of standing in a cemetery.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A כהן may not become טמא from the dead, and graves give over טומאה, so אליהו should not be there.

steps.title: Graves of non-Jews do not give over טומאה
steps.stepSummary: אליהו answers with the ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן יוחי: graves of non-Jews do not make a person טמא, because only Jews are called 'אדם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Hasn't the Master learned טהרות? As it was taught: רבי שמעון בן יוחי says that graves of non-Jews do not make a person טמא, as it says: 'And you, My sheep, the sheep of My pasture, are אדם.' You are called 'אדם', and non-Jews are not called 'אדם'.
steps.whatsHappening: אליהו explains that this is a cemetery of non-Jews. According to רבי שמעון בן יוחי, their graves do not give over טומאה, so a כהן may stand there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of טומאה under a roof is written about an 'אדם' who dies in a tent. A פסוק in יחזקאל calls the Jewish people 'אדם', so רבי שמעון בן יוחי learns that this טומאה applies only to Jews. That removes the assumption behind the challenge in step 3.

keyTerms.meaning: The order of the משנה dealing with purity and impurity
As it was taught in a ברייתא

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the well-known source for the view of רבי שמעון בן יוחי that graves of non-Jews do not give over טומאת אוהל, which matters for כהנים in practice.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא מַתְנֵי מָר טְהָרוֹת?
phrases.english: He said to him: Hasn't the Master learned טהרות?

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As it was taught: רבי שמעון בן יוחי says:
The graves of non-Jews do not make a person טמא,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְאַתֵּן צֹאנִי צֹאן מַרְעִיתִי אָדָם אַתֶּם״.
phrases.english: As it says: “And you, My sheep, the sheep of My pasture, are אדם.”
You are called “אדם”,
phrases.notes: This connects to במדבר 19:14, where the טומאה of a tent is said about an 'אָדָם' who dies.

phrases.english: And non-Jews are not called “אדם”.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא מַתְנֵי מָר טְהָרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Removes a hidden assumption: not every grave gives over טומאה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All graves make a כהן טמא, so אליהו should not be in a cemetery.
steps.terutzMaskana: Graves of non-Jews do not give over טומאה, according to רבי שמעון בן יוחי, so a כהן may stand there.

steps.title: רבה בר אבוה admits he has not learned all six orders
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר אבוה says that he has not even mastered four orders of the משנה, so how could he know all six?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: In four orders I am not proficient. Am I going to be proficient in six?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר אבוה explains why he did not know the ברייתא. He has not even mastered the four commonly learned orders, so he certainly has not mastered all six, including טהרות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story now moves from הלכה to רבה בר אבוה's own life. His admission sets up אליהו's next question about why he has not learned more.

keyTerms.meaning: I am able, I am proficient
Six (all six orders of the משנה)

phrases.english: He said to him: In four I am not proficient,
phrases.notes: He means four of the six orders of the משנה, the ones people usually learned.

phrases.english: In six am I going to be proficient?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to אליהו's question 'Hasn't the Master learned טהרות?'
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No, he has not even mastered four orders, let alone all six.

steps.title: אליהו asks him why
steps.stepSummary: אליהו asks why he has not mastered them.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: And why not?
steps.whatsHappening: אליהו asks why רבה בר אבוה has not learned all the orders. This short question sets up the next move in the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question leads straight to the real problem that אליהו is about to solve. It points the story toward רבה בר אבוה's livelihood.

phrases.english: He said to him: And why not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on רבה בר אבוה's admission.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason he has not mastered the six orders.

steps.title: Financial pressure keeps him from learning
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר אבוה explains that he is under pressure.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The matter is pressing for me.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר אבוה answers that he is under heavy pressure, meaning the struggle to make a living. That is why he cannot learn properly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Poverty is the obstacle to his learning. This answer explains why אליהו now brings him to גן עדן.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter presses on me (I am in financial distress)

phrases.english: He said to him: The matter is pressing for me.
phrases.notes: He means he is struggling to make a living.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אליהו's question in step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Financial hardship keeps him from learning.

steps.title: אליהו brings him to גן עדן to gather leaves
steps.stepSummary: אליהו leads him into גן עדן and tells him to fill his cloak with leaves, and he does.
steps.simpleTranslation: He led him and brought him into גן עדן. He said to him: Spread out your cloak, gather and take some of these leaves. He gathered and took.
steps.whatsHappening: To help with his poverty, אליהו takes רבה בר אבוה into גן עדן. He tells him to collect leaves in his cloak, and רבה בר אבוה does so.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The leaves are meant to give him wealth so that he will be free to learn. The story is building toward the problem in the next step.

phrases.english: He led him and brought him into גן עדן.
He said to him: Spread out your cloak,
Gather and take some of these leaves.
He gathered and took.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: אליהו responds to the financial pressure described in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אליהו gives רבה בר אבוה leaves from גן עדן to relieve his poverty.

steps.title: A heavenly voice says he is using up his עולם הבא
steps.stepSummary: As he leaves, he hears a voice: who eats up his עולם הבא like רבה בר אבוה?
steps.simpleTranslation: As he was leaving, he heard a voice saying: Who eats up his World to Come like רבה בר אבוה?
steps.whatsHappening: On his way out, רבה בר אבוה hears a voice criticizing him. Taking these leaves uses up his reward in עולם הבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This voice acts like a challenge to what he just did. The wealth from גן עדן is not free; it is paid for out of his share in עולם הבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Eats up his world (uses up his reward in עולם הבא)

phrases.english: As he was leaving, he heard someone saying:
Who eats up his world
phrases.notes: 'His world' here means his share in עולם הבא.

phrases.english: Like רבה בר אבוה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges his taking of the leaves in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה בר אבוה's taking the leaves of גן עדן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Benefit from גן עדן in this world is taken out of one's reward in עולם הבא.

steps.title: He throws the leaves away but the cloak keeps their scent
steps.stepSummary: He throws the leaves out, but the cloak keeps their scent. He sells it for twelve thousand דינרים and divides the money among his sons-in-law.
steps.simpleTranslation: He shook out his cloak and threw them away. Even so, he brought back his cloak, and the cloak had absorbed the scent. He sold it for twelve thousand דינרים and divided it among his sons-in-law.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר אבוה throws away the leaves so that he will not use up his עולם הבא. Even so, the cloak keeps a wonderful scent, and he sells it for a fortune and gives the money to his sons-in-law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He gives up the leaves, but he still receives something from them. He does not keep the money for himself, since it came from his share in עולם הבא. Instead he gives it to his sons-in-law.
steps.whatToRemember: רבה בר אבוה gave up a reward from גן עדן rather than use up his עולם הבא. Even the leftover scent made him rich, and he gave that money away to his sons-in-law.

phrases.english: He shook out his cloak and threw them away.
Even so, he brought back his cloak,
The cloak had absorbed the scent.
He sold it for twelve thousand דינרים,
He divided them among his sons-in-law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: His reaction to the heavenly voice in step 9, ending the story.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: He gave up the leaves, but their lingering scent still brought him wealth, which he gave away to his sons-in-law.

steps.title: A poor man's collateral may not be kept overnight, but a rich man's may
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes the פסוק 'If he is a poor man, do not sleep with his collateral' and infers that with a rich man, one may lie down.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: 'If he is a poor man, you shall not sleep with his collateral.' This implies that if he is rich, you may lie down.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic opens with a ברייתא that reads a פסוק about collateral and draws an inference about a rich borrower. The wording sounds odd, and the גמרא will ask about it next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only mentions an עני, so the ברייתא infers that a עשיר is different. But read literally, 'you may lie down with' a rich man's collateral sounds like permission to sleep on his item, which makes no sense. That puzzle sets up the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Collateral, an item held by the lender as security for a loan

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
"And if he is a poor man,
you shall not sleep with his collateral";
but if he is wealthy, one may lie down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the story of רבה בר אבוה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From the פסוק's mention of a poor man, the ברייתא infers that a rich man's case is different.

steps.title: What does the ברייתא mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא is trying to say, since 'a rich man, one may lie down' is unclear.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for an explanation of the strange wording in the ברייתא. This question sets up רב ששת's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is not an attack on the ruling. It asks how to read the words so they make sense, because 'lying down with' a rich man's collateral cannot be meant literally.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he saying? (asks for the meaning of an unclear text)

phrases.english: What is he saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the wording of the ברייתא in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How to understand 'a rich man, one may lie down with his collateral'.

steps.title: רב ששת: 'Do not lie down while his collateral is with you'
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that the meaning is: do not go to sleep while a poor man's collateral is still with you. With a rich man, you may go to sleep while you still hold it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: This is what he means. 'If he is a poor man,' do not go to sleep while his collateral is with you. But if he is rich, you may go to sleep while his collateral is with you.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the question by rereading the words. The point is not 'sleeping on' the item but 'going to sleep while you still have it.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of 'sleep with his collateral' (בעבטו), read it as 'sleep while his collateral is with you' (ועבוטו אצלך). For a poor man, you must give the item back before night. For a rich man, there is no such duty, so you may keep it overnight.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means (introduces an explanation of a text)

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
This is what he is saying:
"And if he is a poor man":
do not lie down while his collateral is with you.
But if he is wealthy,
lie down while his collateral is with you.

steps.whatToRemember: A poor man's collateral must be returned before you go to sleep. A rich man's collateral may stay with the lender overnight.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא means 'do not sleep while his collateral is with you'. The duty to return it at night applies only to a poor man.

steps.title: A confusing ברייתא about taking collateral from a borrower
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a lender may not take collateral, is not obligated to return it, and transgresses all these prohibitions.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: One who lends to his friend may not take collateral from him, and is not obligated to return it to him, and he transgresses all of these prohibitions.
steps.whatsHappening: A second ברייתא is quoted, and it seems to contradict itself. The גמרא is setting up a question about its meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he is not allowed to take the collateral, how can it be that he does not have to give it back? It is also unclear which part 'transgresses all these prohibitions' refers to.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One who lends money to his fellow
is not permitted to take collateral from him,
and is not obligated to return it to him,
and transgresses all of these names.
phrases.notes: 'Names' means the different Torah prohibitions about collateral.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ברייתא on a related collateral topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lender may not take collateral. As written, the ברייתא also seems to say he need not return it, and that he violates all the collateral prohibitions.

steps.title: What does this ברייתא mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the ברייתא, since its clauses seem to clash.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how to make sense of this ברייתא. Two different explanations follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The clash is between 'not permitted to take' and 'not obligated to return'. If taking is forbidden, it should have to be given back. The גמרא wants the correct reading.

phrases.english: What is he saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the wording of the ברייתא in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can the lender be forbidden to take collateral and yet not have to return it? Which clause does 'transgresses' go on?

steps.title: רב ששת: If he took it, he must return it
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת reads the ברייתא as: he may not take collateral, and if he did, he must return it. 'Transgresses all these prohibitions' refers to the last case, where he took it and did not give it back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: This is what he means. One who lends to his friend may not take collateral, and if he did take it, he must return it. 'He transgresses all these prohibitions' goes on the last part.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת fixes the reading so there is no contradiction: taking is forbidden, and returning is required. The prohibitions are violated when he keeps the item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת reads 'not obligated to return' as 'obligated to return' once he has taken it. He then attaches 'transgresses all these prohibitions' to that last clause: a lender who keeps the collateral breaks all the related prohibitions.

keyTerms.meaning: And if he did take collateral from him
The latter clause of a teaching

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: This is what he is saying:
One who lends money to his fellow
is not permitted to take collateral from him,
and if he took collateral from him,
he is obligated to return it to him.
And "he transgresses all of these names"
refers to the latter clause.
phrases.notes: Meaning the case where he took the collateral and didn't give it back.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: הָכִי קָאָמַר, הַמַּלְוֶה אֶת חֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Taking collateral is forbidden, and if taken it must be returned. The prohibitions are violated by not returning it.

steps.title: רבא: The rule depends on when the collateral was taken
steps.stepSummary: רבא agrees he must return collateral taken later, but says collateral taken at the time of the loan need not be returned. 'Transgresses all these prohibitions' refers to the first clause, the ban on taking collateral.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This is what he means. One who lends may not take collateral, and if he took it, he must return it. When is this said? When he took it not at the time of the loan. But if he took it at the time of the loan, he does not have to return it. 'He transgresses all these prohibitions' goes on the first part.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a different reading of the same ברייתא. He keeps the words 'not obligated to return' by applying them to a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא splits the cases. Collateral taken later, to pressure payment, must be returned. Collateral taken when the loan was given is part of the deal and need not be returned. He attaches 'transgresses all these prohibitions' to the opening ban on taking collateral, not to the case of keeping it.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case is this said? (narrows a rule)
At the time of the loan
The first clause of a teaching

phrases.english: Rava said: This is what he is saying:
One who lends money to his fellow
is not permitted to take collateral from him,
and if he took collateral from him, he is obligated to return it to him.
In what case is this said?
Where he took collateral from him not at the time of the loan;
but if he took collateral from him at the time of the loan,
he is not obligated to return it to him.
And "he transgresses all of these names" refers to the first clause.

steps.whatToRemember: רב ששת: collateral must always be returned, and the prohibitions go on keeping it. רבא: collateral taken at the time of the loan need not be returned, and the prohibitions go on the taking.
steps.confusionAlert: Both רב ששת and רבא explain the same ברייתא, but they disagree on two points. רבא says collateral taken at the time of the loan need not be returned, while רב ששת makes no such split. They also disagree about which clause 'transgresses all these prohibitions' belongs to: the end (אסיפא) or the beginning (ארישא).
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, competing answer to the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Collateral taken after the loan must be returned. Collateral taken at the time of the loan need not be. The prohibitions refer to taking collateral.

steps.title: רב שיזבי: One פסוק is about a night garment, the other about a day garment
steps.stepSummary: רב שיזבי teaches before רבא that 'until sunset you shall return it' refers to a night garment, and 'return it at sunset' refers to a day garment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שיזבי taught before רבא: 'Until the sun sets you shall return it' is about a night garment. 'You shall surely return the collateral when the sun sets' is about a day garment.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching splits two פסוקים about returning collateral between two kinds of garments. This sets up רבא's challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One פסוק says to return it 'until sunset', which means during the day. The other says 'at sunset', which means at night. רב שיזבי assigns the first to a night garment, so it would be returned by day, and the second to a day garment, so it would be returned at night.

keyTerms.meaning: A garment worn during the day

phrases.english: Rav Sheizevi taught before Rava:
"Until the sun sets you shall return it to him":
this is a night garment;

phrases.aramaic: ״הָשֵׁב תָּשִׁיב לוֹ אֶת הַעֲבוֹט כְּבוֹא הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ״ –
phrases.english: "You shall surely return to him the collateral when the sun sets":
this is a day garment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching about the timing of returning collateral.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'until sunset' פסוק refers to a night garment, and the 'at sunset' פסוק refers to a day garment.

steps.title: רבא: This is backwards. Why give a day garment at night?
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects: why does the borrower need his day garment at night, or his night garment during the day?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: A day garment, why do I need it at night? And a night garment, why do I need it during the day?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges רב שיזבי's teaching because it seems to return each garment at the time it is not used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason for returning collateral is so the poor man can use the item when he needs it. As taught, the day garment comes back at night and the night garment by day, which gives no benefit. So the teaching seems reversed.

phrases.english: He said to him:
A day garment, why do I need it at night?
And a night garment, why do I need it during the day?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: דִּימָמָא בְּלֵילְיָא לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב שיזבי's teaching from step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב שיזבי's assignment of the two פסוקים to night and day garments.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Returning a garment at the time the borrower does not use it serves no purpose, so רב שיזבי's teaching as worded makes no sense.

steps.title: Should I erase this teaching?
steps.stepSummary: After רבא's objection, רב שיזבי asks whether he should erase his teaching altogether.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שיזבי said to רבא: Should I erase it?
steps.whatsHappening: רב שיזבי heard רבא's objection and asks whether his teaching is so wrong that he should stop teaching it. This question sets up רבא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא showed that רב שיזבי's version makes no sense, because nobody needs a day garment at night. So רב שיזבי asks whether the whole teaching should be dropped, or whether it can be saved by reading it a different way.

keyTerms.meaning: Should I erase it? (Should I stop teaching it?)

phrases.english: He said to him: Should I erase it?
phrases.notes: This is רב שיזבי talking to רבא about the teaching he just recited in Step 18.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רבא's objection in Step 19 by asking whether the teaching should be thrown out.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the teaching so wrong that it must be erased, or can it be saved?

steps.title: רבא flips the two פסוקים: day garment and night garment
steps.stepSummary: רבא says not to erase it. He reverses the reading: 'until sunset' is a day garment taken at night, and 'at sunset' is a night garment taken by day.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: No. This is what it means: 'Until the sun goes down you shall return it to him' is a day garment, which may be taken as collateral at night. 'You shall surely return the collateral to him when the sun goes down' is a night garment, which may be taken as collateral by day.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא keeps the teaching but switches which פסוק goes with which garment. Now each garment is returned exactly when the borrower needs it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Until sunset' means the item has to be with the borrower the whole day, so it must be a day garment. The creditor may hold it only at night. 'Return it at sunset' means the borrower needs it for the night, so it is a night garment that the creditor may hold during the day. This answers רבא's own objection from Step 19.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (a rereading of a text)
A garment used during the day

steps.whatToRemember: A day garment is held by the creditor at night and returned for the day. A night garment is held by day and returned at sunset.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with רב שיזבי's original version in Step 18. רבא flips it, and רבא's version is the one that stands.

phrases.english: He said to him: No,
this is what it is saying:
"Until the sun goes down you shall return it to him"
this is a day garment
which may be taken as collateral at night,
"You shall surely return the collateral to him
when the sun goes down"
this is a night garment
which may be taken as collateral by day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב שיזבי's question by saving the teaching with a reversed reading.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading of the teaching: the garment assignments are switched.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Until sunset' meant a night garment and 'at sunset' meant a day garment, which made no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Until sunset' is a day garment held at night. 'At sunset' is a night garment held by day.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical rule for when each kind of collateral garment goes back to the poor borrower.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: after the debtor dies, the creditor may take it from the children
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that if the debtor dies, the creditor may take the collateral away from the children. He does not have to keep returning it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: If he took collateral from him and the debtor died, he may pull it off his children's backs.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רבי יוחנן teaches that the duty to keep returning the collateral ends when the debtor dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the debtor was alive, the creditor had to give the garment back whenever the debtor needed it. רבי יוחנן says this duty does not pass to the heirs, so the creditor may take the item and keep it.

keyTerms.meaning: He pulls it away (takes it back)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
If he took collateral from him and he died,
phrases.notes: The one who died is the debtor, not the creditor.

phrases.english: he pulls it off from upon his children.
phrases.notes: Literally 'off the backs of his children.' The creditor may take the garment back from the heirs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the collateral rules after the debtor dies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once the debtor dies, the creditor need not return the collateral to the heirs and may take it from them.
steps.whyThisMatters: This statement is the target of the challenge that follows.

steps.title: Challenge begins: רבי מאיר's question in a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to challenge רבי יוחנן with a ברייתא in which רבי מאיר asks why collateral is returned if it was taken.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: רבי מאיר said: But since one takes collateral, why does he return it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to attack רבי יוחנן. This step only starts quoting it, so it sets up the next moves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר seems to ask what the point is of taking collateral if it must keep being returned. Before the challenge can land, the גמרא will first fix the wording of his question.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (from a ברייתא)

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Rabbi Meir said:
But since one takes collateral,
why does he return it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge against רבי יוחנן's ruling in Step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that the creditor may take the collateral from the heirs.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא of רבי מאיר will be shown to clash with רבי יוחנן. The full attack comes in the next part of the ברייתא.

steps.title: How can רבי מאיר ask why we return it? The Torah says to!
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised by the wording of רבי מאיר's question, since the Torah clearly commands returning the collateral.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does he return it?! The Merciful One said to return it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to question the wording of the ברייתא. Asking 'why return it?' makes no sense when the Torah openly commands it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Returning the collateral is a clear Torah command, so it is not something to question. That means רבי מאיר's question cannot mean what it seems to say, and it needs a different wording.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One (ה׳, in the Torah)

phrases.english: Why does he return it?!
The Merciful One said: Return it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the ברייתא quoted in Step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of רבי מאיר's question in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A Torah command does not need to be questioned, so the question as worded cannot be right.

steps.title: Corrected wording: since he has to return it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rewords רבי מאיר's question: since he must return it, why take collateral at all? The rest of the question continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, read it this way: Since he must return it,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording of רבי מאיר's question. This line is only the start, and the question finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is not why the item is returned. Its starting point is the fact that it must be returned, and from there רבי מאיר asks what purpose taking it serves.

phrases.english: Rather: since he returns it,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 24 by rewording רבי מאיר's question.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר was questioning why collateral is returned at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר takes the return as a given and starts from it: since it must be returned, he asks what follows.
